definition: Reprove means to scold or correct, usually gently.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word reprove. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know reprove should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: With one raised eyebrow and two soft words, the conductor reproved the trombones for rushing.
Remind is gentler than reprove — it carries no criticism at all, just a nudge that the rule exists, while a reproof makes real disapproval plain.
Chew out goes further than reprove — the volume rises and the anger shows, while a reproof stays gentle enough to thank someone for afterward.

To scold is the everyday word for telling someone off — often louder, hotter, and aimed more at venting than at fixing anything. To reprove is cooler and more deliberate: disapproval made plain while everyone's dignity stays intact, so the behavior changes and the relationship survives.

To correct is to fix the behavior with no feeling in it at all — a coach adjusting a grip, an editor repairing a comma. To reprove adds the moral note: the person is told, gently but unmistakably, that they earned some disapproval.

In this unit's disapproval family, each word takes a different object: reprove a person, gently, for an act; repudiate a claim or belief, formally and entirely; repulse a physical advance; and save reprobate for the character past correcting.
If the correction could plausibly end with a thank-you, it was a reproof.
